official_facts.fact: NEET-PG 2026: 180 MCQs, 5 sections of 36, 42 minutes per section, sections lock, +4/-1/0.
NEET-PG 2026: from 1 Oct 2026 candidates see question IDs, numerical answer identifiers, their responses and marks in their own login; question text is not published.
NEET-PG 2025: NBEMS published the answer key after Supreme Court orders (29 Apr 2025); questions were not disclosed.
INI-CET: AIIMS does not release an official or provisional answer key.
FMGE: no official question paper PDF; sources conflict on whether an answer key is shown in candidate logins.
FMGE June 2026: NBEMS introduced video-based questions (real clinical recordings); the demo test included them; NBEMS has not confirmed a count.

A_foundational.name: Acid-base and electrolyte disorders
A_foundational.rationale: Underpins nephrology, critical care, endocrinology and toxicology; the same reasoning (anion gap, compensation, sodium/potassium algorithms) recurs across subjects and question formats.

A_foundational.name: Shock, resuscitation and trauma assessment
A_foundational.rationale: Primary survey, GCS and shock physiology link surgery, anaesthesia and medicine; two related concepts appear in this dataset (NEET-PG 2025, INI-CET May 2026).

A_foundational.name: Antimicrobial choice, toxicity and resistance
A_foundational.rationale: Drug-bug matching and signature toxicities connect pharmacology, microbiology and clinical medicine.

A_foundational.name: Cell injury, inflammation and neoplasia (including translocations)
A_foundational.rationale: General pathology is the base for systemic pathology and haematology; two translocation concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A_foundational.name: Autonomic pharmacology and toxidromes
A_foundational.rationale: Receptor pharmacology explains drug effects, poisoning syndromes and perioperative care.

A_foundational.name: ECG and arrhythmias
A_foundational.rationale: Physiology of conduction to bedside ECG diagnosis and management; image-based in many formats.

A_foundational.name: Screening tests, biases and study designs
A_foundational.rationale: Needed to read any evidence and frequently calculation-based; two related concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A_foundational.name: Obstetric emergencies (PPH, eclampsia, shoulder dystocia, cord prolapse)
A_foundational.rationale: Time-critical algorithms with high clinical stakes; four related concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A_foundational.name: HIV and tuberculosis
A_foundational.rationale: Spans microbiology, pharmacology, medicine and national programmes; two related concepts appear in the 2025 recall list.

A_foundational.name: Endocrine emergencies (DKA, adrenal crisis)
A_foundational.rationale: Physiology-driven management with clear algorithms; adrenal insufficiency appears in the 2025 recall list.

C_underrepresented.name: Sepsis and septic shock: recognition and first-hour care
C_underrepresented.rationale: High clinical importance; no observation in this dataset, which says more about the dataset's size than about the exam.

C_underrepresented.name: Anaphylaxis
C_underrepresented.rationale: Life-threatening emergency with a single first-line drug and dose; not observed in this dataset.

C_underrepresented.name: Acute ischaemic stroke: thrombolysis eligibility and time windows
C_underrepresented.rationale: Guideline-dependent and clinically critical; not observed in this dataset.

C_underrepresented.name: Neonatal resuscitation and newborn care
C_underrepresented.rationale: Algorithmic and important; appears only as a coaching forecast (S03), not as an observation.

C_underrepresented.name: Medical ethics, consent and the 2024 criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA)
C_underrepresented.rationale: India's criminal laws changed on 1 July 2024, so older section numbers in books are outdated; syllabus relevance is high and historical data cannot reflect it yet.

C_underrepresented.name: Snakebite and common poisonings
C_underrepresented.rationale: Common in India with specific antidotes and protocols; not observed in this dataset.

C_underrepresented.name: National health programme updates (e.g. TB elimination, NCD screening)
C_underrepresented.rationale: Programmes change often; current versions matter more than historical frequency.

C_underrepresented.name: Video-assessable clinical skills (gait, movement disorders, examination signs)
C_underrepresented.rationale: FMGE introduced video questions in June 2026 (S12). No NEET-PG video questions are reported, so this is a hypothesis about format spread, not a finding.
